title: Buy Now, Pay Later Loans Will Soon Affect Some Credit Scores
summary: AP wire article explains why FICO's new scoring model will soon factor BNPL loans into credit scores and the risks that raises.

assertions.quote: Scoring company FICO said Monday that it is rolling out a new model that factors the short-term loans into their consumer scores.
So far, there's been little visibility into this practice in the industry, and the opacity has led to warnings of
missed payments can hurt or ding a score
Women of color are also more likely to use the loans
the average BNPL loan is for $135, and that repaying such small loans, even consistently, might not result in changes to a credit score that would significantly move the needle

verdicts.note: Matches the Consumer Federation of America's own estimate that a ~$135 average loan has limited capacity to move a score meaningfully.
KC Fed endnote: the average BNPL purchase amount is $926, versus $2,095 for general-purpose credit-card-linked installment plans.
